editorial:
Imagine a world where lying is a family business. You get to follow Zien, a smooth-talking con artist who spends his days making and selling fake Buddhist amulets to gullible people. Then there is his nephew, Riang, who is basically a younger version of Zien but with a massive gambling habit. The whole vibe is chaotic and funny, focusing on how these two try to stay one step ahead of the law and their own bad luck. It feels like a wild ride where you are just waiting to see who gets tricked next and how they plan to dig themselves out of the holes they dug.

The acting is great because the chemistry between the uncle and nephew feels real and snappy. While the plot can get a bit messy at times, the fast pacing keeps you from getting bored. If you like comedies about criminals who aren't actually very good at being criminals, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the end, the schemes finally catch up with them, and the lies start to fall apart in a big, messy way. Zien and Riang realize that their obsession with quick money and fake luck has left them with nothing. They have a heart-to-heart moment where they decide to stop the scams. The movie wraps up with them finding a way to be honest, showing that family is more valuable than any fake amulet.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heist comedies and funny family dynamics.
